name: גַּמְלִיאֵל
gloss: God has dealt bountifully with me; or my recompense is God
summary: Borne by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, the leader of Manasseh in the wilderness, who stood with Moses at the numbering, brought Manasseh’s offering on the eighth day and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:10; 7:54; 10:23); and in the New Testament by the Pharisee and teacher of the law who counselled the council to let the apostles alone, at whose feet Paul was brought up (Act 5:34; 22:3). It joins the root of גָּמַל “deal out to, deal bountifully with” to אֵל, God: “God has dealt bountifully with me”, as the psalmist says Yahweh גָמַל עָלָי (Psa 13:6); or, with the noun גְּמוּל, “my dealing, my recompense, is God”. His father’s name פְּדָהצוּר, “the Rock has redeemed”, is the same kind of sentence.

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, גַּמְלִיאֵל בֶּן־פְּדָהצוּר.
For Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
The leader of the sons of Manasseh, camped beside Ephraim on the west.
On the eighth day Gamaliel brings Manasseh’s offering (to 7:59).
“A Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, held in honour by all the people.”
Paul, “brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel”.
“I will sing to Yahweh, for he has dealt bountifully with me (גָמַל עָלָי)”: the verb the name is formed from, with God as its subject.
“Forget not all his dealings (גְּמוּלָיו)”: the noun, of God’s benefits.

note: BDB key c.cj.af (Num 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59; 10:23). The Peshitta spells the New Testament Gamaliel גַּמַלִיאֵל (SEDRA lexeme 586), and Abbott-Smith gives Γαμαλιήλ as the Hebrew גַּמְלִיאֵל, so TIPNR’s Gamaliel@Act.5.34 is included as a bearer of the same name. Whether the first element is the verb with ־ִי as a joining vowel or the noun גְּמוּל with “my” is not settled by any verse; both readings are given.
